slides.title: A user with a company
slides.subtitle: One user, one company, from a first question to an approved exchange and sign-out
slides.notes: Ada's jacket is not warm enough, and she asks her personal agent, Atlas, to exchange it at Manzanita Outfitters. This example is the whole journey, with every PAP feature it needs, end to end.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph ADA["Ada's side, trusted"] direction TB U["Ada"] -- "asks, approves" --> A["Atlas host
ES256 identity, credentials"] end subgraph CO["Manzanita, reference company"] direction TB D["Device page
Ada signs in here"] -- "same Session" --> API["Company API
Reactor contributions"] end ADA -- "PAP over HTTP" --> CO ADA -. "plain words only" .-> M
slides.caption: Both sides come from this SDK, and no model sits in the protocol path.
slides.notes: On the left, Ada's trusted side: Ada asks and approves, and the Atlas host, with its real ES256 identity, holds every credential. On the right, Manzanita, the reference company assembled from Reactor contributions: its company API, and the device page where Ada signs in herself, for the same Session. Atlas and Manzanita talk real HTTP over ASGI in one process, with no network. Off to the side, the model gets the story in plain words and is never in the protocol path.

slides.title: Getting to a conversation

items.title: Signed-out Session
items.detail: A `Poppy-Session` JWT, signed by a delegated key

slides.notes: Atlas discovers Manzanita and starts a signed-out Session, with a JWT on each request signed by a short-lived delegated key. When Ada asks about her order, Manzanita answers in the conversation with an authorization event: insufficient_scope, with the scope the request needs, which only a signed-in Session can have.

slides.title: Signing in on the company's page

items.title: Poll
items.detail: Signed-in Session and an Account Token

slides.notes: Atlas asks for Device Sign-In on the same Session. Atlas tells Ada where to go. She enters the code and approves on Manzanita's own page. Atlas polls, and the Session is now signed in, with an Account Token.

slides.title: The exchange

items.title: Ada approves
items.detail: This revision, in the host's interface

slides.notes: The conversation carries on, now signed in. Manzanita proposes an Operation with a revision and terms. Atlas shows the summary and terms, Ada approves that exact revision, and Atlas makes the same request again with her approval.

slides.title: Performed once, then signed out
slides.diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
  state "Signed-out Session" as SO
  state "Signed in, Account Token" as SI
  state "Narrowed to orders:read" as N
  state "Token revoked" as R
  [*] --> SO
  SO --> SI : Device Sign-In
  SI --> SI : approval sent again, same answer
  SI --> N : refresh, narrowed
  N --> R : sign me out
slides.caption: Rights come with sign-in, shrink to what is needed, and go at sign-out.
slides.notes: Follow what Atlas holds, from the top. After discovery it has a signed-out Session. Ada signs in on Manzanita's page, and the same Session is now signed in, with an Account Token. Look at the loop: Atlas sends the same approval again, as a network retry would, and gets back the original response, so the exchange happened once. Then it refreshes the Account Token narrowed to orders:read, and when Ada says sign me out, it revokes the token.

slides.title: What the model sees

left.heading: In plain words
items: What Manzanita did, in its own words

slides.notes: The model gets the story in plain words, so it can explain the proposal to Ada. It never sees a code, token, delegation or proof, and it cannot approve anything: Ada approves in the host's interface.

slides.title: One feature per step
slides.notes: Each step of the journey is one feature with its own page. Follow those pages when you want the detail of a single step.
